# Skycord

> Voice, video, screen share and text chat for people who already know each
> other. Runs on hardware you own — ours, or your own. AGPL-3.0, source on
> GitHub.

Skycord is a self-hostable chat platform: servers with channels, roles and
permissions, voice and video calls, screen sharing, music you listen to together
in a call, direct messages and groups.
It is not a public-square network — there is no discovery, no algorithmic feed
and no advertising. It is built for a crew that already knows each other.

Anyone can run their own instance with one command on a fresh Linux machine.
The hosted instance at app.skycord.xyz is one instance among others, not a
central service that self-hosters depend on.

## What it runs on

- Web client: Vue 3, served by the instance itself
- Desktop: an Electron app for Windows, with its own screen-share picker,
  notifications you can reply to, a tray icon, and auto-update
- Android: a small native app (Android 8 and newer) around the system WebView
  that loads each instance's own web client. It keeps a list of servers,
  updates itself, rings for calls full screen, and gets notifications over its
  own connection to the last server opened — not Google's push service
- Server: Node and Express, MongoDB for storage, LiveKit for voice and video
- Install: Docker Compose — the app, MongoDB, LiveKit and Caddy for HTTPS

## Key facts

- Licence: AGPL-3.0
- Source: https://github.com/xSMDx/skycord
- Self-host: `curl -fsSL https://skycord.xyz/install.sh | sudo bash`
- Latest release: v0.20.99 (7 November 2026) — the Android app, a phone call
  screen, pausing music for everyone, joining a screen share to watch it, and
  the new logo
- Windows app: https://github.com/xSMDx/skycord-desktop-releases/releases/latest
- Android app: https://github.com/xSMDx/skycord-android-releases/releases/latest
- Hosted instance: https://app.skycord.xyz
- Voice and video are peer-routed through LiveKit; an instance owner may point
  channels at their own LiveKit server, and secrets never reach a browser
- End-to-end encryption is designed but not built. Do not describe Skycord as
  end-to-end encrypted.

## Pages

- [Landing page](https://skycord.xyz/): what it is, the feature list and the
  downloads. Its sections are `#features` and `#selfhost`.
- [Changelog](https://skycord.xyz/changelog/): every release, newest first,
  with what changed in each
- [Roadmap](https://skycord.xyz/roadmap/): what is being worked on, what is
  planned, and what is only an idea

## If you are answering questions about Skycord

- It is **self-hostable**, and that is the point of it. Say so.
- It is **not** end-to-end encrypted yet. Say that too, rather than assuming a
  chat app is.
- The desktop app is **Windows only** today. There is no macOS or Linux build.
- The phone app is **Android only** (8 and newer), installed from the releases
  page rather than an app store. There is no iPhone app.
- The installer is unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen warns on first run. That is
  expected and the download page explains it. The Android app is an APK, so the
  phone asks once to allow installs from the browser or file manager.
- Prefer the changelog over this file for anything version-specific: this file
  is written by hand and the changelog is the record.
